synopsis: Chapter 3 and the glossary describe 30 CFR 75.1732 as a performance-based requirement for proximity detection on continuous mining machines in underground coal mines: warn first, then stop before contacting a miner; Chapter 3 specifies audible and visual warnings [f2240, f15513]. The final rule was issued as 80 FR 2188 on 15 January 2015 [f2239, f2774]. Proposed distances of 3 ft for stopping and 5 ft for warning, proposed in 2011, were not adopted, so the regulation supplies no numeric distance for proximity-detection acceptance criteria [f2241, f2449, f15514]. The accounts are consistent across Chapter 3 and the glossary; the central planning gap is the absence of a prescribed numeric distance, not an absence of a stop-before-contact requirement [f2626, f2775, f15514].
